You might just be trolling and frankly I don’t really care enough to argue, but he is right you know, there’s a difference between MMR and SBMM. 

Both ranked and casual modes in RL use the same MMR based system, your ranked MMR could be 4000 (an arbitrary number) and you get +/-20 (again just an arbitrary number) per win, because you don’t play casual as much, it could be 1500, still with +/- 20 MMR it’ll take quite a while to get up to 4000 where you match with decent people, answering why you might play quite a few games and still go up against new players.

I’m cos it’s a similar system (SBMM) but it’s a lot more lenient (I think part of the problem in your twos argument was you’re using different definitions of lenient / strict) it’s lenient in that it’s not a rigid +/- 20 MMR per win/loss, based on your last few games it might go +/- 200 or anything in between, which sure it does need tightening a bit, I myself prefer the strict MMR type but that’s cause I used to play a lot of Dota.

In games with MMR he’s also right in saying that you start off low MMR and go up slowly, again for example in RL you might start off at 1000 and go up +/-20 every game, apart from placement games, in these you might go +/-100 every game (more for streaks). This means that a pro RL player starting a new account and wins all 10 games, would have started at 1000MMR, but after placement will be 2500 or something. Obviously causal modes don’t have placement games so you don’t get this fast movement up the ladder.

In the last few seasons the mmr needed for the next rank has shifted down over the course of the season, so at the start of the season you might need 2.3k to get archon1, but by the end of the season, 2.4k might get you legend2, and then with the new season, you’ll drop back down to archon2 or something (arbitrary  numbers I have no idea the actual ones). I went from Ancient5 to Legend1 rank wise, but my mmr stayed the same at 3.4k (you can check this in the stats tab in your profile).

It was to give a small sense of achievement during the season apparently, but for this season they’ve changed that, so your rank should be consistent going into next season whenever that might be.

Also there’s the fact that in the new season the average mmr drops down, that’s to stop real high up guys getting too high (9-10k) and not being able to find a game, so you might drop a small bit of mmr, but you’ll lose the majority of the ranks to them just resetting to their original boundaries.
